Bhikkhuvagga 25. Mendicants The Monk Chapter

Pañcabhikkhuvatthu

Cakkhunā saṁvaro sādhu, Restraint of the eye is good; Excellent is restraint of the eye, sādhu sotena saṁvaro; good is restraint of the ear; excellent is restraint of the ear, Ghānena saṁvaro sādhu, restraint of the nose is good; excellent is restraint of the nose, sādhu jivhāya saṁvaro. good is restraint of the tongue. excellent is restraint of the tongue,

Kāyena saṁvaro sādhu, Restraint of the body is good; excellent is restraint of the body, sādhu vācāya saṁvaro; good is restraint of speech; excellent is restraint of speech, Manasā saṁvaro sādhu, restraint of mind is good; excellent is restraint of the mind, sādhu sabbattha saṁvaro; everywhere, restraint is good. excellent is restraint in every situation. Sabbattha saṁvuto bhikkhu, The mendicant restrained everywhere A monk who is restrained in every situation sabbadukkhā pamuccati. is released from all suffering. is freed from all suffering.

Haṁsaghātakabhikkhuvatthu

Hatthasaṁyato pādasaṁyato, One restrained in hand and foot, Hand restrained, foot restrained, Vācāsaṁyato saṁyatuttamo; and in speech, the supreme restraint; speech restrained, restrained to the utmost, Ajjhattarato samāhito, happy inside, serene, appreciating introspection, concentrated, Eko santusito tamāhu bhikkhuṁ. solitary, content, I call a mendicant. one who is content like this is called a monk.

Kokālikavatthu

Yo mukhasaṁyato bhikkhu, When a mendicant of restrained mouth, A monk who has a restrained mouth, mantabhāṇī anuddhato; thoughtful in counsel, not restless, who gives advice without arrogance, Atthaṁ dhammañca dīpeti, explains the text and its meaning, illuminates the meaning and the Dhamma, madhuraṁ tassa bhāsitaṁ. their words are sweet. and their speech is like honey.

Dhammārāmattheravatthu

Dhammārāmo dhammarato, Delighting in the teaching, enjoying the teaching, Appreciating the Dhamma, approving of the Dhamma, dhammaṁ anuvicintayaṁ; contemplating the teaching, investigating the Dhamma, Dhammaṁ anussaraṁ bhikkhu, a mendicant who recollects the teaching remembering the Dhamma, saddhammā na parihāyati. doesn’t fall away from the true teaching. a monk does not fall away from the true Dhamma.

Vipakkhasevakabhikkhuvatthu

Salābhaṁ nātimaññeyya, A well-off mendicant ought not look down One should not disdain what one has, nāññesaṁ pihayaṁ care; on others, nor should they be envious. nor envy what belongs to others; Aññesaṁ pihayaṁ bhikkhu, A mendicant who envies others a monk who envies the belongings of others samādhiṁ nādhigacchati. does not achieve immersion. does not attain concentration.

Appalābhopi ce bhikkhu, If a mendicant is poor in offerings, Even if a monk has little, salābhaṁ nātimaññati; the well-to-do ought not look down on them. but does not disdain what he has, Taṁ ve devā pasaṁsanti, For the gods indeed praise them, the angels praise him, suddhājīviṁ atanditaṁ. who are tireless and pure of livelihood. the one who lives with purity and diligence.

Pañcaggadāyakabrāhmaṇavatthu

Sabbaso nāmarūpasmiṁ, One who has no sense of ownership When there is nothing whatsoever in mind and body yassa natthi mamāyitaṁ; in the whole realm of name and form, that one thinks of as “mine,” Asatā ca na socati, who does not grieve for that which is not, and one does not sorrow on account of the unpleasant, sa ve “bhikkhū”ti vuccati. is said to be a mendicant. then one can be called a monk.

Sambahulabhikkhuvatthu

Mettāvihārī yo bhikkhu, A mendicant who meditates on love, A monk who maintains benevolence, pasanno buddhasāsane; devoted to the Buddha’s teaching, and who has serene faith in the teaching of the Buddha, Adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ, would realize the peaceful state, arrives at the peaceful path saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ. the blissful stilling of conditions. and the happiness of complete tranquility.

Siñca bhikkhu imaṁ nāvaṁ, Bail out this boat, mendicant! Bale out this boat, monk; sittā te lahumessati; When bailed out it will float lightly. when emptied, it moves easily. Chetvā rāgañca dosañca, Having cut off desire and hate, Having cut off passion and hatred, tato nibbānamehisi. you shall reach extinguishment. go from here to Nibbāna.

Pañca chinde pañca jahe, Five to cut, five to drop, When five are cut off and five are discarded, pañca cuttari bhāvaye; and five more to develop. and another five are developed, Pañca saṅgātigo bhikkhu, When a mendicant slips five chains then a monk who has gone beyond five attachments “oghatiṇṇo”ti vuccati. they’re said to have crossed the flood. is said to have crossed the flood.

Jhāya bhikkhu mā pamādo, Practice absorption, don’t be negligent! Meditate, monk, do not be negligent; Mā te kāmaguṇe ramessu cittaṁ; Don’t let the mind delight in the senses! do not let your mind swirl in sensuality. Mā lohaguḷaṁ gilī pamatto, Don’t heedlessly swallow a hot iron ball! Do not negligently swallow a metal ball, Mā kandi “dukkhamidan”ti dayhamāno. And when it burns, don’t cry, “Oh, the pain!” complaining about suffering as you burn.

Natthi jhānaṁ apaññassa, No absorption for one without wisdom, There is no Jhāna for one who has no wisdom; paññā natthi ajhāyato; no wisdom for one without absorption. there is no wisdom for one who does not reach Jhāna. Yamhi jhānañca paññā ca, But one with absorption and wisdom—One who has both Jhāna and wisdom sa ve nibbānasantike. they have truly drawn near to extinguishment. is close to Nibbāna.

Suññāgāraṁ paviṭṭhassa, A mendicant who enters an empty hut In an empty hut, santacittassa bhikkhuno; with mind at peace a monk with a peaceful mind Amānusī rati hoti, finds a superhuman delight appreciates the absence of humans sammā dhammaṁ vipassato. as they rightly discern the Dhamma. and sees the Dhamma clearly and correctly.

Yato yato sammasati, Whenever they are mindful When one directly experiences khandhānaṁ udayabbayaṁ; of the rise and fall of the aggregates, the appearance and disappearance of the components of being, Labhatī pītipāmojjaṁ, they feel rapture and joy: one acquires euphoria and joy, amataṁ taṁ vijānataṁ. that is freedom from death for one who knows. aware of the deathless.

Tatrāyamādi bhavati, This is the very start of the path This is the starting point idha paññassa bhikkhuno; for a wise mendicant here: for a monk: Indriyagutti santuṭṭhi, guarding the senses, contentment, guarding the sense-faculties, contentment, pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro. and restraint in the monastic code. and restraint according to the code of conduct.

Mitte bhajassu kalyāṇe, Mix with spiritual friends, If one associates with good spiritual friends suddhājīve atandite; who are tireless and pure of livelihood. who live a pure and diligent life, Paṭisanthāravutyassa, Share what you have with others, if one is polite in speech ācārakusalo siyā; being skillful in your conduct. and wholesome in conduct, Tato pāmojjabahulo, And when you’re full of joy, then one will have abundant joy dukkhassantaṁ karissati. you’ll make an end to suffering. and will put an end to suffering.

Pañcasatabhikkhuvatthu

Vassikā viya pupphāni, As a jasmine sheds Just as a jasmine plant maddavāni pamuñcati; its withered flowers, releases its wilted flowers, Evaṁ rāgañca dosañca, O mendicants, in the same way, monks, vippamuñcetha bhikkhavo. shed greed and hate. let go of your passion and aversion.

Santakāyattheravatthu

Santakāyo santavāco, Calm in body, calm in speech, Peaceful in body, peaceful in speech, santavā susamāhito; peaceful and serene; peaceful in mind, and well-concentrated, Vantalokāmiso bhikkhu, a mendicant who’s spat out the world’s bait a monk who has expelled the world's bait “upasanto”ti vuccati. is said to be one at peace. is said to be at peace.

Naṅgalakulattheravatthu

Attanā codayattānaṁ, Urge yourself on, Admonish yourself, paṭimaṁsetha attanā; reflect on yourself. investigate yourself; So attagutto satimā, A mendicant self-controlled and mindful a monk who is self-protected and mindful sukhaṁ bhikkhu vihāhisi. will always dwell in happiness. lives happily.

Attā hi attano nātho, Self is indeed the lord of self, You are your own protector, ko hi nātho paro siyā; for who else would be one’s lord? for who could protect another? Attā hi attano gati, Self is indeed the home of self, You are your own destiny; tasmā saṁyamamattānaṁ; so restrain yourself, therefore, restrain yourself, Assaṁ bhadraṁva vāṇijo. as a merchant his thoroughbred steed. as a merchant restrains an excellent horse.

Vakkalittheravatthu

Pāmojjabahulo bhikkhu, A monk full of joy A monk with abundant joy pasanno buddhasāsane; trusting in the Buddha’s teaching, and serene faith in the Buddha's instructions Adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ, would realize the peaceful state, arrives at the peaceful path saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ. the blissful stilling of conditions. and the happiness of complete tranquility.

Sumanasāmaṇeravatthu

Yo have daharo bhikkhu, A young mendicant A young monk yuñjati buddhasāsane; devoted to the Buddha’s teaching, who makes a sincere effort in following the Buddha's instructions Somaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti, shines upon this world, brightens this world, abbhā muttova candimā. like the moon freed from clouds. like the moon emerging from clouds.

Bhikkhuvaggo pañcavīsatimo.
